summary: Turn Point Light, Stuart Island: an 1893 lens lantern on a post at the turn in Haro Strait, replaced by a 1936 concrete tower; automated in 1974 and managed by BLM.

lens.note: Present 300 mm light dates from 1936 (archive, LighthouseFriends).

structures.note: Lens lantern on a post close to the point (LighthouseFriends); the Board report calls it a tubular-lantern light.
44 ft from base to lantern center (archive).
Two keepers each had one side of the duplex (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Open year-round; reached only by water craft (BLM). Grounds open; dwelling and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). A two-mile walk from the Prevost Harbor dock.

facts.agency: Bureau of Land Management (manager); U.S. Coast Guard (owner)

events.note: Congress appropriated $15,000 for the light and fog signal (act of 3 March 1891).
Contract for the dwelling, fog-signal building, barn and water tanks signed 27 December 1892.
Dwelling, fog-signal building and barn finished by July 1893 (Board report for 1894).
Station began operation on 30 November 1893.
Daboll trumpet fog signal began operation 30 November 1893.
Tug Enterprise ran aground on rocks near the station on the evening of 16 February 1897.
Keepers freed the tug, and a barge its crew had cut loose was found and its occupants brought ashore by breeches buoy.
Oil-burning engines for the fog signal ordered and shipped on 8 June 1899; hot-air engines judged too weak.
Hot-air engines replaced by two oil engines; a 960-gallon redwood cooling tank built.
Keeper L. A. Borchers towed a disabled launch with three men aboard to a place of safety (item in the fiscal 1921 list; the date is not given).
Head keeper Louis A. Borchers died in September 1923 while keeper.
Two 300 mm lens lanterns with electric lamps; characteristic white occulting 2.5 s, eclipse 3 s, white 2.5 s, eclipse 3 s, red 1 s, eclipse 8 s, every 20 s (Bulletin, January 1930).
Small concrete tower with 300 mm light; the archive gives tower established 1936.
Diaphragm foghorn replaced the Daboll trumpet.
Coast Guard took over the lighthouses (society history).
Photograph captioned in LighthouseFriends shows the station with a World War II lookout tower.
Furnace in the officer-in-charge quarters exploded on 22 December 1955; he was taken to Prevost to meet a Coast Guard helicopter.
Station automated; dwelling later used by University of Washington researchers studying whale migration.
Work on the roofs of the fog-signal building, dwelling and barn; windows restored with wavy glass.
Bureau of Land Management and the Turn Point Lighthouse Preservation Society signed a cooperative management agreement.

corrections.why: The record lists the standing tower as built in 1893, with 6.1 m height. The archive gives the present concrete tower as established in 1936, with the 300 mm light; the 1893 light was a lens lantern on a post.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record has 1893 (archive, Rowlett) and 1936 (Wikidata). Both are right for different structures: the first light, a post lens lantern lit 30 November 1893, and the present concrete tower of 1936.
The record has Fl W 2.5s; LighthouseFriends says the light flashes white every two and a half seconds today. The OpenStreetMap entry Fl 2.5s omits the colour.

notes_for_editor: 1) First light: the Board's 1894 report says 'tubular-lantern light'; LighthouseFriends says a lens lantern on a post; the society quotes the 1892 plan for a fixed white lens lantern on a tripod platform. The story gives these. 2) The 1930 Bulletin describes two 300 mm lanterns with electric lamps and a 20-second characteristic, which predates the 1936 tower that the archive and LighthouseFriends give. The sources do not explain it; the story says so. 3) Engine power: LighthouseFriends says two 14-horsepower oil engines; the 1900 Board report's power figure is garbled in the OCR, so no horsepower appears in the story. 4) Record tower height 6.1 m vs archive 44 ft (13.4 m) from base to lantern centre; the record's height and built year are the most likely to be wrong. Only the built year is proposed as a correction. 5) Archive says Keeper's Quarters? No but gives 1893 wood; LighthouseFriends and the society describe the duplex in use. No change proposed. 6) Roster variants: LighthouseFriends spells Edvard L. Muller, John A. Jimmerfield, Guy Martin, and gives Charles Mykol 1940-1943; the archive gives Edward L. Muller, John A. Jimerfield, Guy C. Martin and 1939-1943. The roster spelling is kept. 7) Auld's flag: the Bulletin index credits William Auld with the Turn Point efficiency flag; the 1925 Bulletin list is column-garbled and places a different name next to Turn Point. LighthouseFriends says Auld received the flag for 1924 and 1925. 8) The 1897 tug Enterprise rescue rests on LighthouseFriends and the society's note of the commendation. A Chronicling America search for Turn Point with Enterprise in Washington papers 1896-1898 gave no hits. 9) The 1891 appropriation list heading is garbled in the OCR; the page header reads second session of the fifty-first Congress, and the story uses that. The checker should read the page image for the heading. 10) The Board's 1888, 1891 and 1892 reports quoted by the society are not in our corpus and are cited through the society. 11) Fiscal years: the Board volume labelled 1893 holds the fiscal 1893 report (scan 241), and the one labelled 1894 holds the fiscal 1894 report (scans 310 and 555). The 1896 paragraph is in the report for the year ended 30 June 1896. 12) Commissioner fiscal 1921 item (scan 668): inside the fiscal year 1921 list of assistance to vessels; the date of the launch rescue is not given. 13) OCR: the Bulletin 1918 fish list (San Juan Island sardines etc.) is garbled; only clean phrases are quoted. Hoover's letter is quoted from clean OCR words. 14) National Register: not checked. The record has no NRHP number. Wikipedia was not cited. 15) Visiting: LighthouseFriends says grounds open, dwelling and tower closed, a two-mile walk from Prevost Harbor; BLM says the site is open year-round and reached only by water craft; the record says not open to the public. The story follows BLM and LighthouseFriends. 16) Living people: Douglas W. Force (officer in charge 1955-1956) is named as LighthouseFriends names him in the 1955 incident; his service ended before 1960. Coast Guard keepers from the 1960s and later appear only in the roster. Keepers named in the prose all left before 1960; later keepers appear in the roster only. 17) Keeper family details (Christiansen's children, Wheeler's daughter) come from the society and LighthouseFriends; the story gives only the dates and facts they print. 18) Verification 2026-10-27: first-run quote check found all 109 quotes (none missing). Changes to the story: 'turn sharply north' replaced by LighthouseFriends' 'make a hard right' (the source gives no northward turn); the route sentence now follows LighthouseFriends (Strait of San Juan de Fuca, Haro Strait due north) instead of the San Juan channel; the lens-lantern sentence now carries its footnote. Checked against LighthouseFriends, the Turn Point Light History (society PDF, which quotes the 1888, 1891 and 1892 Board reports and the 1893 and 1894 reports), the BLM page, the USLHS record (roster: 130 lines, all matching roster.py, person slugs included), the Light-House Board volumes (1891 scan 24; 1893 scan 241; 1894 scans 310, 311, 555; 1896 scan 203; 1899 scan 246; 1900 scan 227), the 1918 Bulletin p. 22 (Borchers, Bureau of Fisheries, Hoover's letter to the Secretary of Commerce, all confirmed), the 1930 Bulletin p. 6, the 1924-1929 index pp. 2 and 36 (Auld, efficiency flag), and the 1921 Commissioner list (scan 668). The 1899 shipping date (8 June) and the 1900 oil-engine entry are confirmed on the page text. Personal details (Wheeler's daughter, the Brooks census household) are printed by the society or LighthouseFriends; the keepers named are dead or left service before 1960 (Force, 1955-1956, is the latest). 19) Note 9 resolved: the page image (scan 24, printed p. 17) confirms the heading 'Appropriations made at the second session of the fifty-first Congress for light-house purposes' and the line 'Turn Point light and fog-signal station, Washington ... 15,000', matched by its line in the list (not by column).
